ground_truth.title: Top 6 Slack alternatives for team collaboration
ground_truth.main_content:
If you haven't used Slack before, chances are you've at least heard of it within business circles. This app has transformed how teams communicate, blending instant messaging, file sharing, and collaboration into one workspace. Add on a user-friendly interface, and you've got yourself the most popular digital communication tool for years running.

But Slack is not always the perfect match for everyone. Some teams need simpler tools, others want tighter integration with project management apps, and some just want a more affordable or distraction-free option.

That’s why we've dedicated this article to exploring which Slack alternatives are best for your needs. Whether you’re a freelancer looking for chat tools or part of a company ready for something more structured, there are plenty of platforms worth considering.

And when paired with IFTTT, you can take your communication and automation to the next level. Our powerful tool connects over 1000 apps and services to keep your workflow running smoothly. Read on to see exactly how we pull this off, and all the information you'll ever need to make an informed decision on a Slack alternative.

Why look for different communication platforms?

Slack is a great solution for real-time communication, but even its most dedicated users acknowledge some common drawbacks. This isn't to say that Slack is a bad choice; in fact, we use it every day here at IFTTT. Instead, these drawbacks might be significant enough to your unique needs that it's worth looking elsewhere.

For starters, Slack's free plan has limited message history, and paid plan pricing can get steep as teams grow. If your team is very large, or you are planning to expand in the near future, it's worth considering how adding more users may affect your channels or overall organization within the app.

On the other end of the spectrum, notification overload can make staying focused difficult for small powerhouse teams. If you find yourself struggling to keep conversations organized and direct, exploring alternatives might open the door to a more efficient setup.

Modern chat tools go far beyond just messaging, offering voice and video calls, integrated task management, and smart notification controls. Choosing the best one is a matter of finding what features are most important. Next, we'll dive into six Slack alternatives that bring equally robust communication options to the table: you can't really go wrong with any of them.

Top Slack alternatives for better communication

Quickly, before we start, we'd like to add a note about how IFTTT's Applet system works. Our platform uses a simple "If This Then That" logic to build automations, and these little pre-packaged connections are known as Applets. They'll be scattered throughout this article, and if you see one you like, just click on it to get started. We'll talk about how to create your very own custom Applet soon.

Now, let's take a look at the six top Slack alternatives that can forever reshape the way you communicate with your team.

1. Microsoft Teams

Pricing: Free plan available; Microsoft 365 Business Basic $6/user/month; Business Standard $12.50/user/month.

Microsoft Teams is arguably the most well-known alternative to Slack, particularly for organizations already using Microsoft 365. It combines chat, video conferencing, document sharing, and app integration in one hub, making it ideal for teams that live in Word, Excel, or Outlook.

The platform’s deep integration with Office apps and OneDrive makes collaboration straightforward. Channels and threads keep discussions organized, while its built-in meeting tools rival Zoom in both quality and functionality.

Simply put, if you are already comfortable with the Microsoft ecosystem, you'll feel right at home with Teams.

2. Discord

Pricing: Free; Discord Nitro $9.99/month.

Originally built for the gaming and hobbyist community, Discord has evolved into one of the most flexible communication platforms for small and large teams alike. Its combination of voice, video, and text channels makes it a great choice for creative teams or groups that value simple, casual collaboration.

Discord’s unique server and channel-based organization gives teams the freedom to structure conversations however they like. It supports custom roles, permissions, and bots, making it surprisingly powerful for business or creative work.

Don't rule out this tool for your professional needs!

3. Google Chat

Pricing: Free with Google Workspace; Business Starter $7/user/month; Business Standard $14/user/month.

Similar to Microsoft Teams, those deeply invested in Google’s ecosystem will like Google Chat. The app offers a clean, minimal, and integrated experience that can be picked up right away. Since it's part of Google, it works seamlessly with Gmail, Meet, and Drive, creating a unified space for collaboration.

Google Chat organizes discussions into Spaces where teams can share files, assign tasks, and jump into video meetings instantly. The real advantage lies in how tightly it connects with other Google Workspace tools, so there’s virtually no friction when switching between messaging, meetings, and more.

4. Twist

Pricing: Free plan available; Unlimited plan $6/user/month.

If Slack feels too noisy, Twist offers a calmer, more focused alternative. Built by the creators of Todoist, Twist was designed around asynchronous communication, meaning it encourages thoughtful, organized discussions instead of rapid-fire chat. This very grounded take on team communication shows real benefits for certain types of teams.

Conversations in Twist happen through threads, not cluttered timelines, which makes it easier to find information later. It’s ideal for remote teams who don’t need to be “always on,” and who value deep work and clear communication.

5. Chanty

Pricing: Free plan available; Business plan $3/user/month.

Chanty is a lightweight and very affordable Slack alternative that offers just the right mix of simplicity and features. It supports group chats, threads, audio calls, and built-in task management, plus an intuitive interface that’s easy to navigate.

Chanty’s strength lies in how it blends quick communication and productivity. You can turn any message into a task, assign it to a teammate, and track progress without ever leaving the chat window. That makes it an excellent option for small to mid-sized teams looking for structure without complexity.

6. Mattermost

Pricing: Free (self-hosted); Professional Cloud $10/user/month.

For teams that prioritize privacy and self-hosted solutions, Mattermost is an excellent alternative to Slack. It’s open-source and fully customizable, which means you have control over where your data lives and how your communication environment is configured.

Mattermost offers the familiar channel-based chat layout but adds features like role-based access control, custom integrations, and deep DevOps compatibility. It’s a favorite among technical teams who want the flexibility to adapt their tools to their workflow.

How IFTTT enhances team communication

No matter which tool you choose, IFTTT helps you connect it to the rest of your digital ecosystem. With over 1000 supported services, it can turn your communication hub into the fully automated workflow tool you've been dreaming of.

Imagine automatically posting a message when a deadline approaches, sending a daily summary of completed tasks to a chat channel, or logging team updates in Google Sheets without typing a thing. That’s the magic of automation, and how IFTTT helps you save time, reduce manual errors, and keep everyone in sync.

Getting started is free, and it only takes five minutes. Just log into IFTTT, explore existing Applets like we discussed earlier, or create your own. Building an Applet is also easy to pick up, and is based on our "If This Then That" logic. For a complete guide on getting started, visit our new user blog here.

How to choose the right Slack alternative

Picking the right tool can be the difference between ultimate productivity and just, meh. The best tool for you depends on your team’s size, goals, and communication style. However, here are a couple of general things to consider:

- Integration needs: Are you already tied to Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace?

- Team size: Small teams might prefer Chanty or Twist, while larger ones benefit from Teams or Mattermost.

- Communication pace: Do you need real-time chat or more asynchronous discussions?

- Budget: Free plans go a long way for smaller groups, while premium tiers unlock advanced collaboration features.

Automate, collaborate, and simplify with IFTTT

At the end of the day, communication tools should make your life easier. Slack set a high bar, but its alternatives each bring something unique to the table, whether that’s better focus, affordability, privacy, or integration depth.

Pairing these platforms with IFTTT elevates them even further, connecting chat, tasks, and apps across your digital workspace. Whether you’re a freelancer running a solo operation or part of a large distributed team, automation helps you stay efficient, informed, and in control.
